skill.name: when-chaining-agent-pipelines-use-stream-chain
skill.description: Design and run chained agent pipelines with sequential, parallel, and streaming data flow patterns.
skill.summary: Guides agent pipeline design, execution, monitoring, and validation with Claude Flow commands.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: The confirmed risks are documented command examples that run npx claude-flow@alpha and may create files, spawn agents, or monitor pipelines. Several static detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences and ASCII pipeline diagrams. No evidence of prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or hidden malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: External package execution through npx claude-flow@alpha
remediation.suggestion: Pin a trusted package version, document package provenance, and require user confirmation before any command is run.
Keep the workflow as documentation unless the user explicitly asks to execute it. Add dry-run guidance and expected file outputs.
Separate non-executable diagrams from bash examples and label executable commands clearly for safer agent interpretation.

content.value_statement: Agent workflows can lose context when each stage runs separately. This skill shows how to connect stages, pass outputs, monitor streams, and validate results.
actual_capabilities: Defines sequential, parallel, and hybrid agent pipeline patterns.
Shows Claude Flow commands for designing pipeline stages and data flow.
Explains memory and stream channels for passing stage outputs.
Provides execution, monitoring, metrics, and validation steps.
Lists success criteria, performance targets, and common issue fixes.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow and a working npx environment.
Does not provide executable source code beyond command examples.
Uses placeholder input files that users must create.
Does not verify external package integrity or installation safety.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Research-To-Code Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan stages where research findings become analysis inputs, then code inputs, tests, and review material.

use_cases.title: Stream Multi-Agent Outputs
use_cases.description: Use memory or stream channels to pass live outputs between specialized agents during a larger workflow.

use_cases.title: Validate Pipeline Results
use_cases.description: Collect outputs, compare expected results, and create validation reports after a pipeline run.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a three-stage research, code, and test pipeline for my repository. Include stage inputs, outputs, and success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Stages With Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to define memory-based handoffs between five agent stages. Include keys, stored outputs, retrieval points, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor a Streaming Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a monitoring plan for a stream-based agent pipeline. Include throughput, latency, backpressure, and error-rate checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Adaptive Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design an adaptive agent pipeline that mixes sequential and parallel stages. Include dependency rules, failure handling, and result validation.

output_examples.input: A team wants research, coding, testing, and review agents to work in order.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a staged pipeline plan with clear handoffs, connection steps, execution strategy, and validation criteria.

output_examples.input: A workflow needs live output from one agent to feed another agent.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends stream channels, monitoring metrics, and backpressure checks for the live handoff.

output_examples.input: A release process needs evidence that all pipeline outputs match expectations.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines result collection, comparison, validation reporting, and performance targets.

best_practices: Define stage inputs, outputs, and validation rules before spawning agents.
Use memory channels for durable state and streams for live handoffs.
Monitor throughput, latency, backpressure, and error rates during execution.
anti_patterns: Running every stage in parallel without checking dependencies.
Passing unvalidated outputs into later agents.
Ignoring package trust and environment permissions before using npx commands.

faq.question: What does this skill help automate?
faq.answer: It helps design and operate chained agent pipelines where each stage passes outputs to later stages.

faq.question: Does it require Claude Flow?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples rely on Claude Flow commands executed through npx.

faq.question: Can it support parallel pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes sequential, parallel, and hybrid patterns with dependency-aware execution.

faq.question: How are outputs passed between agents?
faq.answer: The skill explains memory-based handoffs for stored state and stream-based handoffs for live data.

faq.question: Does it validate final results?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes result collection, schema validation, expected-output comparison, and validation reporting steps.

faq.question: What security care is needed?
faq.answer: Users should trust and pin external packages before running npx commands from the examples.
